The present conflict brings a warning: We’re just starting to wrestle with the dangerous consequences of our new missile age, writes AEI’s @HalBrands 
bloomberg.com/opinion/articl…

We have to hope that one way or another, President Trump secures an early opening of the Hormuz Strait that would allow the restoration of a more normal energy, fertilizer, aluminum, and helium supply flow from the Gulf.

If that does not occur, we should brace ourselves for a US and world economic recovery, writes AEI’s Desmond Lachman. 
aei.org/economics/a-differen…

When today’s education “experts” dismiss rote memorization, they are ignoring wisdom that had been passed down for millennia, writes AEI’s @MrDanielBuck 

thehill.com/opinion/educatio…

Mandating books is easy. Getting students to read them—and read them well—is the hard part. And that work will not be done in statehouses. It will be done, if it is done at all, in classrooms, writes AEI’s @rpondiscio aei.org/education/should-sta…

The question is whether policymakers calibrate their response to the actual threat—and wisely reassess as new data emerges about benefits and costs—or act preemptively without firm evidentiary support, writes AEI’s @JimPethokoukis on AI’s impact on jobs. aei.org/economics/ai-job-pan…

Want to hear more of @dpletka on foreign policy? Tune into the What The Hell Is Going On podcast each week, where she discusses America's national security challenges with @marcthiessen and top experts. open.spotify.com/show/2Yo2gs…

AEI’s @dpletka: We can do this. We can escort ships through the Strait of Hormuz. But we've got other stuff going on, and that's not a good division of labor. So I am reasonably confident that our European allies are going to come in and help us on this, just as we have come in and helped them on Ukraine.

Video

On the latest episode of Not Dead Yet, @BenSasse and @ChrisStirewalt speak with @prattprattpratt about hard work, the choices parents make, the ups, downs, and idols of success, and how he wants his kids to understand what it means to be a man.

aei.org/multimedia/not-dead-…
The AI chip arms race is changing global supply chains; policymakers need to participate in the discussion, writes AEI’s @ShaneTews aei.org/technology-and-innov…

The war with Iran has revealed an uncomfortable reality:  the US does not look like it can sustain protracted, high-intensity conflict with a near-peer adversary.

Read more of why this is the case and how the US can fix its depleted war stocks:
theamericanenterprise.com/ru…

The executive branch should make maximum use of a powerful existing tool—the Center for Medicare and Medicaid Innovation—to cut health entitlement expenditures, writes AEI’s James Capretta. aei.org/health-care/refocusi…

AEI’s Kori Schake: President Trump may use ground forces to try to force open the Strait of Hormuz or capture Kharg Island or another Iranian territory in order to strengthen his negotiating hand.

Video

What comes next in Iran? 

This week on the What The Hell Is Going On podcast, @DPletka and @MarcThiessen are joined by Israeli Ambassador @yechielleiter to discuss US-Israeli resolve, what objectives remain, and the long-term future of the region. podcasts.apple.com/us/podcas…

AEI’s @ScottGottliebMD joins CNBC’s Squawk Box to discuss why the FDA’s new rare disease framework is an encouraging first step and how FDA can build on the guidance to create a path for the clinical development of new therapies.
